scope.callDepthCaveat: Every 'active-registration-at-traced-call-depth' / 'conditional-registration' classification below describes ONLY the shape of the source call chain this document actually traced: whether a runtime conditional exists between the app's traced entrypoint and the ipcMain.handle/on call for that channel. It is NOT proof the channel is registered in any given running app instance -- an untraced caller further up the chain, a build/platform flag, or a startup failure could still prevent registration in practice. No app, daemon, or test was executed to verify a live process; this is source classification only, explicitly distinguished from behavioral/runtime validation.

methodology: For each of the 66 channels: (1) the exact channel string and original census status were read verbatim from parity-source-bridges.json; (2) `grep -n "'<exact-channel-literal>'"` against the registering file located every line where that literal string appears, distinguishing a DECLARATION line (a local const/array-literal binding the string to a name, if present), a REGISTRATION line (the exact line the literal appears on inside an ipcMain.handle/on call, whether passed directly or via a one-hop wrapper function), and any DISPOSAL line(s) (ipcMain.removeHandler/removeListener/removeAllListeners referencing that same channel or its bound name); (3) the registering function's own call site was read directly to classify it as conditional (behind an `if` on a runtime value) or unconditional AT THE TRACED DEPTH (see scope.callDepthCaveat); (4) disposal was recorded as two INDEPENDENT booleans per record -- reRegistrationGuardObserved (an unconditional removeHandler/removeAllListeners at the top of the SAME registering function, before it re-registers) and explicitEventDrivenDisposerObserved (a removeHandler/removeListener reachable only from a LATER runtime event such as mainWindow.on('closed', ...), confirmed by reading both the disposer definition and its invocation call site) -- a record may have neither, either, or (for macosTccPrompts:*) both, never conflated into one bucket; (5) every testPointerFiles entry was checked with a direct filesystem existence check (not assumed from a prior document) before being cited; a body was never opened to claim coverage, only to confirm the file's presence as a plausible pointer. All 66 records resolved to a real, traced-depth-active-or-conditional project-source registration; 0 fell into 'no handler found after bounded search' or 'genuinely dynamic identity' for this cohort.

records.disposalAnchor: re-registration guard: src/main/window/attach-main-window-services.ts:170 (unconditional ipcMain.removeHandler at the TOP of every registerTccPromptNoticeHandlers() call, before re-registering). SEPARATELY, an EXPLICIT event-driven disposer: mainWindow.on(closed) at line 204 checks activeTccPromptHandlerToken !== handlerToken (lines 205-207, so a stale prior generation closed-handler is a no-op) and, only for the currently-active generation, calls releaseOwnerClaim() (line 208) then ipcMain.removeHandler for this exact channel at line 209, then resets activeTccPromptHandlerToken = null (line 213).
records.disposal: BOTH mechanisms are present and distinct: a re-registration idempotency guard (line 170) AND a genuine mainWindow-'closed'-triggered teardown (line 209), gated by an exact handlerToken match, not by the monotonic counter alone -- the counter only ever increments to mint the next token; the actual authorization gate at invocation time is `ownsNotice` (attach-main-window-services.ts:183-184), which requires `!mainWindow.isDestroyed() && !mainWebContents.isDestroyed() && event.sender === mainWebContents` (exact WebContents identity + liveness, not the token).
